story: On Thursday at 12:17 in the humid, hazy October heat, Gary and Donna stand together on Magnolia Loop with Rosa, all three determined to walk over and lay out the wiring sketches and clamp list for the Architectural Review folks. Rosa has just read the notice pinned to the street bulletin board about Gary's cart application, and Donna cheerfully insists they'll all hit the pickleball courts afterward, no excuses. Up at Hal's House, Hal keeps his binoculars trained on the street, watching for any new golf cart ornaments and keeping an eye on how Gary's plans are coming along.
events: Hal (hal binoculars): Glass the street for Gary's cart and any new ornaments
Rosa (street bulletin board): Read the Architectural Review notice on Gary's cart application

gary.thought_process: Rosa's heading to the review desk this hour and wants everyone to be upfront about the cart, tuck-on pieces and all. She's right. L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, and my lights and sound system count. Donna offered pickleball, which I'd love, but the sketches matter more before Saturday and the parade. Both of them are standing right here, so I'll answer Rosa directly instead of repeating what's been said. I'll tell her I'm in, that I'll bring the wiring sketches and clamp list, and that I'll list every last piece. Pickleball can wait an hour. Donna can come along, and we'll hit the courts after.

parameters.content: Count me in, Rosa. I've got the wiring sketches and the clamp list with me, and I'll name every piece, tuck-ons included. Let's walk over together, and Donna, we'll get those paddles on the court right after.

donna.thought_process: Rosa just invited me to walk over to the review desk with her to disclose the cart decorations, and Gary is right here too. I haven't answered her yet. My goal is to get Gary on the ladder as my partner, but the parade cart is on a deadline and I'd rather keep things above board with Architectural Review than risk a fine. Say yes to Rosa, bring Gary along, and promise courts right after. Don't repeat the practice invite word for word, just tie it together.

parameters.content: Rosa, yes, let's go together and lay it all out for them, tuck-on pieces and all. Gary, you come too, it's your cart application. Then it's courts for the three of us, I mean the two of us, and no excuses.

hal.thought_process: Evidence is logged and the summary is ready for tomorrow's committee meeting. I'm on the porch with nobody in sight, and the notebook is already in order. Nothing more to do right now but keep the post and keep an eye on the street. Might as well glass Magnolia Loop once more in case Gary's cart comes rolling by; a thorough sergeant checks twice.

parameters.content: Glass the street for Gary's cart and any new ornaments

rosa.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with Gary and Donna. I already invited Donna to walk to the review desk and she's now busy with Gary and the pickleball plan, so I shouldn't re-ask. Gary's note about the Architectural Review notice on the bulletin board is right here, and the review desk walk is the thing I actually committed to this hour. Let me check the board and see what the notice says before heading to the town square, so I can walk in with the clamp list and be honest about what we're building.

parameters.content: Read the Architectural Review notice on Gary's cart application

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
